peru.overview: Cusco and the Sacred Valley offer famous trekking, leading through the high Andes to ancient ruins. The multi-day routes are the main draw, led by the four-day Inca Trail to Machu Picchu, which needs a permit booked months ahead, and the demanding, high-altitude Salkantay trek past glacier-capped peaks. Day hikers can tackle the steep, breathless climb to Rainbow Mountain at over 16,000 feet, or explore shorter paths connecting Inca sites above the valley. The best conditions run from May to September, while heavy rains disrupt routes early in the year.

months.8: Another excellent month for multi-day routes and high-altitude day hikes. The dry ground and clear skies make for reliable footing on steep descents, though the landscape turns brown and dusty.

peruvian-amazon.overview: Walking in the Peruvian Amazon means guided excursions from jungle lodges, reached by boat or small plane. Walks are slow, hot, and humid, and focus on the dense rainforest rather than sweeping views. The best access to the forest floor is during the drier months, when trails are less muddy and river levels drop.

piedmont.overview: Piedmont offers two distinct walking landscapes: the rolling vineyard trails of the Langhe and the high alpine routes of Gran Paradiso National Park. Walkers can link wine villages on gentle loops around Barolo, with the Alps visible on clear days, or head north for long mountain day hikes and multi-day treks like the Grande Traversata delle Alpi. The season runs from late spring through autumn.

months.3: Spring begins to thaw the lower valleys, though high alpine routes remain under snow. The vineyard trails around Barolo become pleasant for easy day hikes as temperatures rise.
months.6: Summer opens the high alpine routes in Gran Paradiso for long day hikes and trekking. The Langhe trails grow warm, making early morning starts advisable.
months.11: The alpine hiking season ends as winter snows arrive. The Langhe trails are cold and often foggy, though still walkable between the villages.

months.1: Winter brings freezing temperatures and occasional snow, limiting walks to city parks like Petrin Hill while the sandstone trails are icy and Pravcicka Gate is open only Friday to Sunday.
months.2: Trails in the sandstone gorges remain icy and Pravcicka Gate keeps winter weekend hours, leaving urban parks as the most reliable walking options.
months.11: Pravcicka Gate drops to weekend-only hours as the days grow short and cold, shifting the focus back to easy walks in the city parks.

provence.overview: Provence offers day hiking, from the steep limestone inlets of the Calanques National Park on the Mediterranean coast to the trails connecting the hilltop villages of the Luberon. Routes range from easy coastal paths to long climbs up Mont Ventoux, with the best walking found in the cooler shoulder seasons.

months.2: Late winter remains cool, offering pleasant walking along the coastal paths and lower valleys before the spring warmth arrives.
months.6: Temperatures rise significantly, making early morning starts essential for long routes and exposed coastal paths.
months.11: Late autumn brings cooler temperatures, perfect for exploring the lower valleys and coastal paths.

months.1: The dry season provides the best conditions for the rainforest and mountain trails. Paths are less muddy, and the cooler air makes the steep climbs in the Cordillera Central more comfortable.
months.2: Dry-season weather holds, with firmer paths in El Yunque and the Cordillera Central and cooler mornings for the steep climbs.
months.3: Dry, warm days continue to favor the rainforest and mountain trails, though humidity begins to creep up by afternoon.
months.6: Heat and humidity make the walking heavy. Afternoon thunderstorms are common, turning dirt paths into thick mud, though the shaded canopy of El Yunque offers some relief.
months.7: Heat stays high and storms build most afternoons, so morning walks in El Yunque's shade are the better bet.
months.8: Hurricane season brings heavy rains and a real risk of storm closures, and the trails are often flooded or blocked by debris.
months.9: Peak hurricane season keeps storm closures likely, with flooded trails, fallen debris and heavy humidity making walking heavy going.
months.10: Hurricane risk remains, and the rain-soaked trails are often blocked by debris, with the high humidity making any walk heavy going.

months.1: Winter walking is cool, with temperatures in the 50s. Coastal paths in the Salento and the Gargano forests are open, though sea breezes can be brisk.
months.2: Temperatures remain in the 50s. The trails through the Foresta Umbra and along the limestone cliffs are open, with occasional rain showers.
months.11: November cools into the 60s. The trails remain open, offering pleasant walking before the winter chill arrives.
months.12: December is cool, with temperatures in the 50s. The coastal paths and forest loops stay walkable between showers.

punta-cana.overview: The Dominican Republic offers the highest mountain trekking in the Caribbean, centered on the demanding multi-day route up Pico Duarte. Walkers can also explore the cloud forests of Valle Nuevo National Park and the coastal trails of the Samaná Peninsula. The best conditions for the high-altitude treks and inland day hikes run from December to April, avoiding the heavy rains and intense heat of the hurricane season.

months.1: The dry, cooler weather makes this an ideal month for the demanding multi-day trek up Pico Duarte and exploring the inland cloud forests.
